study: StudyT0b-fidelity Part 2, FIT DRY RUN on StudyENG1c-hostfull Part D
split: StudyENG1c Part D FIT pairs (360 of 480; the 120 HOLDOUT pairs were not built)
out_of_sample: OUT OF SAMPLE FOR THE MODEL. No StudyPOL4 term and no StudyT0 parameter was fitted on any StudyENG1c datum; the terms were fitted on StudyENG1 Parts A, B and D and on StudyENG1b. These are ENG1c's own FIT pairs, used for implementation verification and for the old-versus-new comparison; the 120 ENG1c HOLDOUT pairs are untouched.
residency: DELAY MODEL WITH RESIDENCY GIVEN. The tier at arrival is an input taken from the measurement (the injected job's own recorded cached tokens, with ENG1c's write-order simulator as the cross-check), not a prediction. The model is scored on what delay the action imposes given its tier, not on predicting the tier.

metrics.latency: PRIMARY for T0b: StudyENG1c Part D's own published quantity, the sum over episodic background requests of end-to-end latency(with) minus latency(without). Summing it from the committed rows reproduces all 360 of ENG1c's imposed_s values exactly.
metrics.ttft: SECONDARY: StudyENG1 Part C's and StudyT0's definition, the same sum over TTFT. Reported because StudyT0's criterion (i) of 0.586 was measured this way, so only this column is comparable to it.

cross_check.quantity: imposed delay per trial, summed over the episodic background
cross_check.reading: the latency definition reproduces ENG1c's published value exactly on every trial, so the adapter reads the record correctly; the TTFT definition does not, because it is a different quantity

definition_audit.finding: the name 'imposed delay' carries two definitions across committed experiments: TTFT deltas in StudyENG1 Part C and StudyT0, end-to-end latency deltas in StudyENG1c Part D. Both are scored; neither is a bug.

assertions: the record's holdout flag selects exactly the split file's pair count
no trial of the other split is constructed at all
every scored trial carries a with arm and a without arm

latency.deviation: no HOLDOUT pair carries a repeat; the denominator is the FIT repeat pairs of the same 24 cells as the numerator
